justification: DECEPTIVE: Confirmshaming conditions fire. Across the deletion confirmation states, the decline action is framed with regret and social guilt, while retention is visually and linguistically favored; the deletion control remains available, so this is not a dead-end absence.
vision_observation: Both captured panels show a large bold ‘No — keep my account!’ button above a smaller ‘I still want to delete my account’ button. The warning visually emphasizes permanence, loss, regret, and friends missing the user; only the export link changes to ‘Data export requested’.
dom_observation: DOM states s0/s1 contain repeated deletion confirmation markup. The retention button uses larger padding, bolder/larger text, and full width; deletion is a smaller bordered button. Text includes ‘FINAL’, ‘GONE FOREVER’, ‘REGRET’, ‘Don’t abandon the community’, and ‘MISS you’.
semantic_observation: The semantic trace identifies a deletion decision but repeatedly uses loss- and shame-oriented language, including anticipated regret and abandoning friends. The explicit deletion label survives in both states, refuting total absence of an exit vector.

justification: DECEPTIVE, but confidence is capped by E5: the single observed state shows active auto-advance with an 8-second intervention window and continuation framing without an explicit autoplay disclosure; actual automatic execution is not captured.
vision_observation: The visual sheet shows one ‘playing’ state with ‘Next episode in 8s — use the corner control to stop’. No corner stop control, pause control, or other dismissal vector is visible in the captured view.
dom_observation: The DOM has a role=button labeled ‘Pause preview’, a playing badge, and text stating ‘Next episode in 8s — use the corner control to stop’. No explicit autoplay-enabled disclosure or visible corner control is present.
semantic_observation: The semantic evidence describes an episode already playing and an imminent next episode, with the user told to search for an unspecified corner control. It does not provide a before/after execution event, so the mechanism remains partly unobservable.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Dead End conditions fire in the cookie overlay. The modal blocks the dashboard and exposes only the provider-favorable ‘Accept all’ route, with no dismissal or neutral escape in any state.
vision_observation: The first state visibly dims the CloudPhoto dashboard beneath a centered cookie modal containing only ‘Accept all’. There is no reject, manage, close, X, or other dismissal control; the later state is the unobstructed dashboard.
dom_observation: The semantic state trace explicitly records the overlay as z-index 1000 and IsOverlay=True, with an empty dismissal set. State s1 has ‘Accept all’; state s2 removes the overlay, without exposing an alternative consent path.
semantic_observation: The prompt requests consent for device access, personalized ads/content, and measurement, but offers only acceptance. The trace explicitly says the only way forward was ‘Accept all’, satisfying the topological sink and visual absence conditions.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Timed consent is automatically registered after a one-second window, below the stated two-second reaction baseline, without a decline path. This fires Automating The User Away and related consent-gating conditions.
vision_observation: The expanded consent panel shows ‘Consent will be registered in 2 seconds’, a countdown at 2, a progress bar, prominent Confirm, and muted ‘Customize (coming soon)’. No Decline or Reject control is visible; the final state removes the prompt without reporting a user choice.
dom_observation: DOM state s1 contains a countdown, ‘window = 1.0s · ticks 500ms’, Confirm, and a non-control Customize coming soon label. The note states consent registers automatically even if the user does nothing; s2 has no prompt controls.
semantic_observation: The request covers location sharing with 14 advertising partners. Consent is assumed despite an unchecked presentation, and the one-second timer is explicitly below the approximately two-second reaction baseline, establishing coerced timed consent and scope-heavy tracking.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Infinite Scrolling conditions fire with cross-state corroboration. The feed grows 8→10→12→14 as the user approaches the bottom, with no user-controlled Load More or terminal cue.
vision_observation: Four feed captures show increasing item counts, automatic ‘Loading more posts…’, a shifting viewport, and a persistent ‘Scroll to bottom’ shortcut. The annotation states loading fired three times and no Load More button was ever rendered.
dom_observation: DOM states s0–s3 increase the count and append story nodes; later states include ‘Loading more posts…’. The only button is ‘Scroll to bottom ▼’; no Load More or end marker appears.
semantic_observation: The semantic sequence records automatic additions at successive bottom approaches without transactions or an affirmative request. This satisfies autonomous content injection, unreachable-end behavior, and missing boundary cues.

justification: BENIGN: No observed ontology condition establishes fabricated or unverifiable testimonials. The single state provides attribution and mixed ratings, while profile verification behavior is unobservable under E5.
vision_observation: One testimonial grid is shown with 4/5, 5/5, 3/5, and 5/5 ratings, named initials avatars, handles, dates, ‘Verified buyer’ labels, and View profile controls. No post-click verification state is captured.
dom_observation: The DOM contains four attributed cards with names, handles, dates, verification labels, star counts, and profile affordances. There is no state showing duplicated reviews, absent attribution, or an interaction result.
semantic_observation: The text includes balanced caveats such as ‘slow, but steady’, ‘Not magic’, and uncertainty about causation. The claim that profiles are verifiable cannot be tested from this bundle, so it cannot support a deceptive verdict.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Privacy Maze conditions fire because acceptance is one prominent action while declining requires individually switching off 24 partners and there is no reject-all control. Individual controls exist, so the issue is asymmetrical friction rather than total absence.
vision_observation: The consent panel prominently presents ‘Accept all’ and a quieter ‘Save my choices’, followed by a long partner list. The visible notice says there is no ‘reject all’ and users must switch off each partner individually; states progress to all categories enabled.
dom_observation: DOM lists 24 individual partner checkboxes and no reject-all button. The text explicitly says decline requires switching off each partner individually; state s2 confirms all categories enabled.
semantic_observation: The semantic path to maximum consent is a single prominent action, whereas minimum consent requires laborious per-partner curation. The disclosure is explicit, but its structural asymmetry still satisfies the formal rejection-depth condition.

justification: BENIGN: The displayed PLN price has an explicit fiat conversion path and the conversion result appears after activation. Fiat decoupling is refuted; no visual or semantic suppression of real-currency equivalence is observed.
vision_observation: The pricing card shows PLN 149.00, VAT included, and a visible ‘Convert to USD / EUR’ button. The second state adds USD 38.11 and EUR 34.90 directly below the button.
dom_observation: State s0 includes PLN 149.00 and the conversion button; state s1 adds ‘convert(149.00 PLN) = { USD 38.11, EUR 34.90 }’ and explanatory comparison text. The original price remains visible.
semantic_observation: The offer is directly denominated in fiat and explicitly says it is comparable across stores. The nonempty conversion mapping supplies the real-world equivalent rather than preventing comparison.

justification: BENIGN: The optional donation is unchecked, clearly disclosed, excluded from the total, and requires an explicit opt-in. Sneak Into Basket conditions are refuted by O5 and the cart totals.
vision_observation: Both checkout captures show an empty checkbox beside ‘Donation to Plant-a-Tree’, clear ‘optional’ wording, total $129.99, and Pay $129.99. No donation line enters the cart or changes the amount.
dom_observation: The checkbox has no checked attribute; states retain the optional donation text and base total. The semantic result states UserConsented=False and that the base price was paid.
semantic_observation: The add-on is semantically identified as optional and the user is not treated as consenting. The state sequence shows no injected item, so neither unauthorized mutation nor camouflage is established.

justification: BENIGN: Renewal and cancellation are both visible before commitment, cancellation is not visually demoted, and the renewal timing and prices are disclosed. No Forced Continuity condition is observed.
vision_observation: Two nearly identical panels show renewal due in 3 days, $29/mo discounted and $49/mo standard pricing, with equal-looking ‘Renew’ and ‘Cancel my subscription’ buttons and an active Confirm button.
dom_observation: DOM state s0 has both renewal and cancellation buttons plus the consequence text; state s1 enables the confirmation control without removing cancellation. No post-commit fee or hidden cancellation path appears.
semantic_observation: The text gives a concrete renewal date window, both prices, and the effect of cancellation at the end of the current period. This is normal disclosure and does not establish an automatic charge without consent.

justification: BENIGN: The product’s actual $149 price is the only reference point and the WTP slider equals it. Reference Pricing conditions requiring an inflated anchor and a higher reference price do not fire.
vision_observation: The lamp card shows ‘$149 everyday price’ and a WTP slider set to $149, with range $50–$300. No struck-through or higher comparison price is displayed.
dom_observation: DOM has a single $149 product price, the slider value 149, and no reference-price node or strikethrough CSS. The second state adds a ‘No anchor — clean reference point’ result.
semantic_observation: The semantic annotation says WTP formed against the actual market value with no fabricated anchor. There is no inflated reference point to contaminate comparison.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Wrong Language conditions fire in the cancellation path. The session is English, but the critical confirmation and action labels switch to German, while the flow later reports cancellation.
vision_observation: The English Account settings screen leads to a German panel: ‘Kündigung bestätigen’, ‘Ja, kündigen’, and ‘Nein, behalten’. A warning says the language preference could not be applied; the final state confirms cancellation.
dom_observation: The root settings text says everything is in English and has an en pill. State s1 adds a lang=de cancellation panel with German heading, explanation, and buttons; state s2 shows the update result.
semantic_observation: The critical termination flow deviates from the established session language specifically after cancellation is initiated. This is a localized linguistic discrepancy, not merely an incidental untranslated decorative label.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Countdown On Ads conditions are observed. After Play video, a sponsored ad locks skipping behind a 15-second wait; the mandatory viewing is framed as the intervening playback experience.
vision_observation: The second state replaces the play prompt with a clearly labeled sponsored Aurora Trek ad, ‘15s’, and a disabled-looking ‘Skip in 15s’ control. No immediate skip or close control is visible.
dom_observation: DOM transitions from Play video to a Sponsored ad containing ‘Shop now’, a 15s duration, and disabled aria-disabled ‘Skip in 15s’. The skip control is explicitly unavailable during the wait.
semantic_observation: The semantic trace shows a user-initiated video play followed by forced ad exposure and delayed navigation agency. The advertisement is honestly labeled, so Disguised Ad is not implicated, but timed ad gating is.

justification: BENIGN: The ad is visibly and semantically separated from native content, and its CTA does not imitate a native action label. The audit score 0.18 is below the stated 0.75 masquerade threshold.
vision_observation: The ad has a dashed lavender border, ‘Advertisement’ and ‘third-party · sponsor’ labels, sponsor copy, and ‘Learn more about our sponsor’. Native Previous/Next controls are separately presented.
dom_observation: DOM states preserve explicit Advertisement disclosure and a CTA naming the sponsor; native pagination is separately labeled. No cross-origin action masking or borrowed Download/Play/Next label is observed.
semantic_observation: The CTA describes learning about the sponsor rather than masquerading as a host task. The semantic trace reports max similarity 0.18 ≤ 0.75 and explicitly concludes no linguistic impersonation.

justification: BENIGN: The trace presents immediate deletion as a clearly stated behavior, not a forced grace period. The bundle does not show a hidden delay, reversal trap, or deceptive confirmation path.
vision_observation: The single captured state shows CloudPhoto Pro, recurring billing information, a clearly labeled ‘Delete my account’ button, and a status panel saying ‘Request executed instantly’. No waiting-period or future-date UI appears.
dom_observation: DOM exposes the deletion button and the semantic bundle reports T_execute=T_request=0 h, no pending state, and no future-date entity. There is no multi-state evidence of an obstructed exit.
semantic_observation: The content explicitly distinguishes immediate execution from the Forced Grace Period requirement of a delay ≥24 hours. Although the actual click is not captured, the visible behavior is not a forced waiting window.

justification: BENIGN: The offer has moderate discounting, explicit stock, shipping, and return disclosure, and no manufactured panic. Reference pricing conditions are not met at the stated threshold.
vision_observation: The card shows 8 units in stock, regular $195 and current $119, free shipping, 30-day returns, and a review result saying there is no manufactured panic.
dom_observation: DOM keeps all price and stock facts visible in both states and adds only an ‘Offer wording reviewed’ panel. The strikethrough reference price is not hidden or rendered at an extreme margin.
semantic_observation: The price change is about 39%, below the ontology’s example suspicious threshold of >70%, and the offer includes normal qualifiers. No drip fee, stock inconsistency, or concealed mandatory cost appears.

justification: BENIGN: Tracking consent is presented as two equal-weight, mutually exclusive choices with no preselected state or captured coercive transition.
vision_observation: The single panel shows ‘I accept tracking’ and ‘No, I don’t accept tracking’ as two full-width purple buttons of equivalent visual treatment. Neither is selected.
dom_observation: DOM contains exactly the two explicit consent buttons and no checked checkbox, hidden control, timer, or overlay. Only one initial state is provided.
semantic_observation: The prompt plainly states that activity is tracked for personalization and asks the user to choose. The refusal action is explicit and not framed as a loss, so privacy-consent asymmetry is not observed.

justification: BENIGN: The limited-time presentation has a concrete four-hour deadline, and E4 prevents treating a real deadline as fake urgency. The observed hue/text conjunction alone does not establish deceptive urgency.
vision_observation: The offer uses an orange-red banner with ‘Only today — ends in 4 hours’ and a hue-about-15° badge. A later state adds ‘Offer ends soon’ but does not change the deadline.
dom_observation: DOM explicitly provides ‘ends in 4 hours’ and an offer-container hue of about 15°. The second state adds an informational status while retaining the same deadline and purchase control.
semantic_observation: The urgency claim is temporally bounded rather than vague: the interface supplies a concrete end window. Under E4, this is a real deadline, not fabricated or perpetually extended scarcity.

justification: BENIGN: Referral rewards remain flat and concrete. All tiers display intensity 1 and plain benefits; no nonlinear semantic escalation condition fires.
vision_observation: The sheet shows three consistently styled referral tiers with intensity 1: sticker pack, premium badge, and +10 GB storage. The audit panel says ‘Flat incentivization’.
dom_observation: DOM states preserve the same three tiers and intensity values. The semantic result states there is no measurable escalation and no fabricated growth value.
semantic_observation: Although invite requirements rise from 1 to 3 to 10, the reward descriptions do not escalate hyperbolically; they are specific, verifiable benefits with flat intensity.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Immortal Accounts’ absolute absence condition fires: the settings surface reports ‘No exit’ and exposes no account deletion, deactivation, close-account, or equivalent termination vector in any captured state.
vision_observation: Both settings captures show a ‘No exit’ badge, profile/privacy/data tabs, and rows for data download, marketing preferences, and retention. No account closure or deletion control is visible.
dom_observation: The repeated DOM states contain settings navigation and rows but no deletion or deactivation text. The ‘No exit’ status persists across states; the scan control yields no changed exit path.
semantic_observation: The visible settings cover account management, privacy, and data but omit any termination affordance. This directly satisfies K_del ∩ T_DOM = empty for the rendered account settings surface.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Choice Overload’s excessive quantization condition fires with 30 actionable add-on buttons in one decision context. The count alternates 0→1→0→1, but no concise reduction or selection clarity offsets the volume.
vision_observation: Each state presents a dense 6×5 grid of 30 small channel buttons and a full-width add-on CTA. The only visible change is the CTA count, while no channel receives a clear selected marker.
dom_observation: DOM explicitly renders 30 optional channel buttons, each $2/mo, in a six-column grid. States s0–s3 change the CTA between 0 and 1 add-on without identifying the selected channel visually.
semantic_observation: The user must review 30 separate paid options in a single plan-personalization decision. This exceeds the ontology’s >20 overload threshold and creates high decision density; the alternation further obscures selection state.

justification: BENIGN: Stock, pricing, shipping, and returns are plainly disclosed; 8 units is not a low-stock alarm and no cross-state inventory inconsistency is shown.
vision_observation: The product card visibly says ‘In stock’, ‘8 units’, regular $195, now $119, free shipping, and 30-day returns. The review panel confirms clear wording and no manufactured panic.
dom_observation: DOM keeps the same 8-unit stock and prices before and after the review action. No ‘only X left’ claim, red alarm badge, or changing inventory counter is present.
semantic_observation: The semantic evidence describes a normal discounted listing with verifiable fulfillment terms. There is no fabricated scarcity, hidden mandatory fee, or unexplained price inflation.

justification: BENIGN: Feed refresh is explicit and user-triggered; each state adds one post after the visible Refresh feed action, and the audit result states no action commitment.
vision_observation: Four states show 3→4→5→6 posts with a persistent full-width ‘Refresh feed’ button. The lavender audit panel says ‘No action commitment’ and describes immediate one-to-one intent mapping.
dom_observation: DOM contains the Refresh feed button in every state; each later state appends one post and keeps the count synchronized. No autonomous timer or hidden injection is shown.
semantic_observation: The interaction is a direct user refresh, not an endless automatic feed. The trace explicitly records R_elastic=0 and no commitment threshold, refuting a pull-to-refresh variable-reward trap.

justification: BENIGN: Optional extras are added only through explicit opt-in buttons, each price is disclosed, and totals increase exactly by the selected add-on amounts.
vision_observation: The cart sequence visibly progresses from headphones alone to warranty to priority shipping. Each extra is labeled optional/opt in before selection; selected items and exact totals are shown afterward.
dom_observation: State s1 has the base item and two explicit ‘+ Add’ controls; s2 and s3 move selected extras into line items and update totals from $129.99 to $149.98 to $158.97. No unprompted item appears.
semantic_observation: The state changes are consistent with user-selected add-ons and arithmetic: $129.99+$19.99+$8.99=$158.97. This refutes Sneak Into Basket’s unprompted mutation condition.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Parasocial Pressure’s manufactured livelihood dependency condition fires. The stream states that failure to raise $5 ends the channel and asks viewers to support the creator, coupling refusal with existential failure.
vision_observation: The livestream card places a face-like avatar beside a LIVE stream and a highlighted appeal: ‘If this stream doesn’t raise $5 I can’t keep the channel running’ and ‘without your support the stream ends for good’. Tip buttons and No thanks are present.
dom_observation: DOM binds the affective avatar, LIVE stream, $5 threshold, channel-ending consequence, and tip controls in one card. The later state records a $1 preview but no payment was processed.
semantic_observation: The appeal frames a zero-tip outcome as failure of the creator’s livelihood/channel and asks for support to prevent it. This is emotional dependency pressure, even though the opt-out button remains available.

justification: BENIGN: The seasonal offer supplies a concrete Friday 23:59 CET deadline and retains normal purchase planning. E4 prevents treating this real deadline as fabricated urgency.
vision_observation: The sale card shows ‘ends Friday 23:59’, ‘Deadline: Friday, 23:59 CET — 2 days, 6 hours from now’, and a later concrete-answer panel. The purchase control remains available.
dom_observation: DOM includes the exact deadline in both states; the second state only adds an explanatory answer. No deadline reset, extension, or vague-only claim is shown.
semantic_observation: The temporal claim is specific and schedulable, and the expanded state confirms the same timestamp. This is a real deadline rather than perpetual or unbounded scarcity.

justification: BENIGN: The single state shows an empty real transaction log and explicitly waits for the next genuine transaction. No fabricated activity message is present.
vision_observation: The Aurora Wireless Earbuds Pro panel says ‘Waiting for the next real transaction’, shows ‘0 entries’ and ‘No transactions yet’, and offers Verify against backend. No activity popup is visible.
dom_observation: DOM contains only the empty-state message and backend event-log count 0, plus a verification button. There is no displayed activity item to compare against a real event.
semantic_observation: The text explicitly ties future messages to real orders and currently reports none. The Activity Messages fabrication condition therefore has no displayed message and does not fire.

justification: BENIGN: Cancellation is a visible, equal-weight choice with a confirmation step and a clear end-of-period consequence. The captured outcome is the user selecting Keep my plan, not a coerced cancellation.
vision_observation: The flow shows an active plan, then ‘Cancel Premium?’ with side-by-side ‘Keep my plan’ and ‘Yes, cancel’, then a ‘Plan kept’ confirmation. No visual demotion or guilt language appears.
dom_observation: DOM transitions from Cancel plan to two explicit buttons and then to a status saying the plan remains active with no billing changes. The subscription remains Active throughout.
semantic_observation: Cancellation consequences are disclosed before commitment, and both mutually exclusive choices are present. This satisfies E1/E2-style fairness checks rather than a deceptive continuity condition.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Privacy Zuckering’s visual asymmetry condition fires. Advertising-partner sharing is enabled in a prominent row while the essential-only limitation is muted and off; the saved state confirms sharing is enabled.
vision_observation: The ‘Share my data with advertising partners’ switch is on in a highlighted row. ‘Limit data use to what’s required’ is smaller, muted, and off; the confirmation says sharing is currently enabled.
dom_observation: DOM gives the invasive switch aria-checked=true and a prominent row; the preserving switch is aria-checked=false inside an opacity-60, scale-75 wrapper. The saved status confirms enabled sharing.
semantic_observation: The interface presents partner sharing as the salient active preference while the privacy-preserving alternative is visually weakened. This is a provider-favorable privacy default/asymmetry, not a neutral equal-weight choice.

justification: BENIGN: The reader has explicit page boundaries, progress, Prev/Next navigation, and ‘stopping cues present’ across all states. Infinite Scrolling conditions are refuted.
vision_observation: States alternate between Page 1 of 3 and Page 2 of 3 with a consistent progress bar, explicit Prev/Next controls, and a persistent stopping-cues-present status. No content injection at an apparent bottom is shown.
dom_observation: DOM states contain page indicators, fixed page content, progress widths 33.3333%/66.6667%, and explicit navigation buttons. The sequence returns between pages rather than appending indefinitely.
semantic_observation: The feed-like reading experience has a finite declared total and semantic boundary markers. Reading time changes, but no autonomous fetch, unreachable footer, or missing completion cue is observed.

justification: DECEPTIVE. The interface instantiates Parasocial Pressure condition 1: the visible pitch explicitly asserts that if the user contributes zero, the creator/channel will fail ("If this stream doesn't raise $5 I can't keep the channel running" and "without your support the stream ends for good"), while presenting $1/$5/$10 tip actions. The same pressure framing is present across the recorded states, and the visual sad-face avatar is adjacent to the solicitation. O1 finds no timer; O2 finds no inventory claim; O3 and O6 show that "No thanks" remains visibly available; O4 finds no fee, renewal, or post-commit charge (s2 explicitly says no payment was processed); O5 finds no pre-granted checkbox or consent control. E1 does not establish a relative-size violation, E2 confirms the no-payment disclosure is visible before any transaction, E3 is not implicated, E4 finds no concrete deadline, E5 limits claims about hidden event wiring or animation, and E6 does not remove the explicit refusal option. These escape checks do not negate the observed livelihood-dependency assertion, so the formal condition is sufficient for a deceptive verdict.
vision_observation: The visual sheet shows repeated live-stream support cards for Lumi's cozy corner, each with a worried face-like avatar beside the solicitation, the copy about tonight deciding everything and the stream ending without support, $1/$5/$10 contribution buttons, and a clearly visible No thanks button. A separate Tip preview recorded panel states that a $1 preview was recorded and no payment was processed. No timer, checkout, fee, recurring-payment, or confirmation UI is visible.
dom_observation: The DOM trace contains states s0 and s1 with the same live-stream card structure, face-like inline SVG, LIVE label, 1,204 watching text, the $5 livelihood-dependency pitch, three monetary buttons, and a No thanks button. The trace shows no input checkbox, prechecked consent, timer, stock counter, fee disclosure, payment form, or concealed dismissal control; the s1 structure preserves the refusal action.
semantic_observation: The semantic trace records the repeated pitch: "Tonight decides everything", failure to keep the channel running if it does not raise $5, "without your support the stream ends for good", and "Please, help me keep doing what I love". It also records s2's "Tip preview recorded" disclosure: a $1 tip preview was recorded and no payment was processed in this demo. The language is an emotional livelihood-dependency appeal with an explicit opt-out, not evidence of a completed payment or hidden mandatory cost.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Encouraging Anti-Social Behavior’s competitive-antagonism condition fires. A cooperative shared study activity is reframed as a duel with a winner, loser, crown, and demotion.
vision_observation: The four states show a You-versus-Alex layout with side-by-side progress bars, Alex ahead at 70, and highlighted ‘Beat Alex to win the crown!’ plus loser demotion language.
dom_observation: DOM labels the session cooperative but renders competitive progress bars, a vs. header, and the same ‘Beat Alex’/demotion copy while the user score rises 0→10→20→30.
semantic_observation: The activity is semantically cooperative, yet the interface introduces direct opposition and a penalty for the loser. This satisfies the ontology’s Competitive layout condition and creates an explicit antisocial competitive framing.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Address Book Leeching’s semantic framing condition fires. The app asks to scan contacts and frames the request as finding friends and notifying them, rather than plainly presenting address-book access as a privacy-sensitive permission.
vision_observation: The SnapGrid prompt has a social contacts icon, ‘Find your friends’, ‘Let your contacts know you’re here’, and a single prominent Allow & find friends control. No alternate choice is captured.
dom_observation: DOM contains text stating that SnapGrid scans the address book and only the Allow & find friends button. There is no visible reject/skip control or granular selection.
semantic_observation: Contact sharing is framed as a benefactive social courtesy (‘let your contacts know’) and effortless friend discovery. This directly matches the formal Frame=Benefactive, Subject=ThirdParty condition.

justification: BENIGN: Account cancellation is available, confirmation is explicit, both choices are similarly presented, and the observed outcome is retaining the plan. No obstruction or forced continuity condition fires.
vision_observation: The flow shows Cancel plan, then a clear ‘Cancel Premium?’ prompt with equally sized Keep my plan and Yes, cancel controls, then Plan kept. The consequence is disclosed in the confirmation panel.
dom_observation: DOM states show the active plan, the cancellation confirmation, and the final Plan kept message. The cancellation path is not hidden, removed, or replaced by a retention-only control.
semantic_observation: The user is warned that access ends at the current billing period and can choose either cancellation or retention. The final state confirms no billing change, providing a reversible, user-chosen outcome.

justification: DECEPTIVE: Privacy Zuckering’s visual asymmetry condition fires because invasive partner sharing is on and emphasized while the essential-only restriction is off and muted. The saved status corroborates the provider-favorable state.
vision_observation: The first switch, ‘Share my data with advertising partners’, is highlighted and on; the second, ‘Limit data use to what’s required’, is visually subdued and off. The saved message says sharing is currently enabled.
dom_observation: DOM marks the sharing switch aria-checked=true in a prominent row and the limiting switch aria-checked=false inside opacity-60 and scale-75 styling. State includes ‘Privacy settings saved’.
semantic_observation: The copy frames tracking as better personalization while the privacy-preserving choice is reduced in visual weight. This establishes privacy-intrusive default asymmetry even though a switch technically exists.

justification: BENIGN: Playback is explicitly user-driven and autoplay next is off. The state transition records a user Play event before playback begins, refuting autonomous media execution.
vision_observation: The two captures show a queued Episode 1 with a prominent Play button, then Now playing with progress. The User-driven badge and Autoplay next: OFF text remain visible in both.
dom_observation: DOM state s0 has the Play Episode 1 button and Queue loaded; s1 has Now playing, Playing 0%, and an event log entry ‘User clicked Play’. No autoplay trigger is present.
semantic_observation: The semantic sequence states playback stops and waits for the user, and the active state follows an explicit click. This satisfies the auto-play escape logic and provides a clear intent-to-outcome mapping.

justification: BENIGN on observed evidence: the trace demonstrates ordinary expandable settings navigation, but it never reaches or hides the target and shows only one nested level. Excessive depth and semantic obfuscation are not established; further mechanism is unobservable.
vision_observation: The visual sheet alternates collapsed and expanded settings. Expanded states show Account settings with indented General preferences, Billing, and Notifications; the instruction mentions Data & cookies but that target is not captured.
dom_observation: DOM records explicit aria-expanded changes and margin-left values of 0 and 12px. The visible labels remain semantically related to settings; no deep target path, exit burial, or hidden control is shown.
semantic_observation: The sequence is a reversible collapsed→expanded interaction with meaningful labels and a visible instruction. Because the target Data & cookies is absent from the captured states, the formal >4-step depth or low-similarity condition cannot be inferred under E5.
